headline: Army Paid Twice, Everything Else Paid Nothing At All
paragraphs: Twelve games reached the grader, three got a polite pass, nine drew action, and ten tickets went out at ten dollars apiece. Three came back. The week closed 3-7 for a loss of 41.82 on 100 staked, an ROI of negative 41.8 percent, against a model that walked in expecting to hit 59.5 percent. Confidence and competence filed separate returns this week and only one of them was audited.

The entire profitable portion of the afternoon lived in Tulsa. Army +2 at a claimed 64 percent and a five point edge cashed for 9.09, and the matching Army ML +100 returned a clean ten after the 38-35 finish. Liberty -9 hiding behind a 34-6 scoreline was the other winner. The worst of it was Over 47.5 in Duke at Virginia, a 62 percent conviction and a 4.3 point edge that watched 19-16 happen in real time.

Spreads carried the damage at 2-6 and negative 52.3 percent, which is most of a week in one market. Of the ten plays whose lines moved, exactly two moved toward the model, so the market and the ledger agreed about who was wrong. Season now sits at 123-148-6 across 277 plays and five real weeks, down 263.09 at negative 9.5 percent, with an expected 60 percent meeting an actual 45.4. The excluded hindsight week shows 40-25-1 and plus 110.47, which proves only that picking games after they end is easy.
